name: Cellulite cup (Cellulite suction)

card.summary: A handheld suction cup massaged over the thighs and buttocks to smooth the look of cellulite dimpling.

quick.overview:
A cellulite cup is a silicone or plastic cup that creates suction on the skin. Users glide it over areas such as thighs and buttocks hoping to smooth dimpled skin.

It is a consumer take on suction and massage methods, which are one of the non-invasive cellulite approaches listed in medical references.
quick.how: Typically used with massage oil, moved over the skin in strokes. Cupping in general leaves cups on for 5 to 15 minutes or slides them with oil.
quick.risks: Cupping breaks capillaries and can cause bruises, scarring, burns, discolouration and pain; it may worsen eczema or psoriasis.

lead: A cellulite cup applies suction to skin; it is used in the hope of smoothing cellulite dimples.[1] Suction or massage is classed among non-invasive mechanical cellulite treatments.[1]
Cupping, the older practice, uses suction cups and has produced mixed research; some reviews find low-to-moderate evidence for pain reduction.[2]

angle.text: Users apply it to areas with dimpling hoping for a smoother look. Effects are described as temporary by users.

paras: Cupping breaks capillaries under the skin, causing bruises (petechiae and purpura), and can cause scarring, burns, discolouration and pain.[2] The NCCIH notes it may worsen eczema or psoriasis.[2]

No studies found for cellulite cups specifically. Wikipedia notes cellulite can resist treatments, and lists suction or massage as non-invasive therapy.[1] Reviews of cupping in general report poor study quality.[2]
